ChoYong LC100 Review

The most feature-packed radio I've reviewed on this site — a genuine internet radio with Wi-Fi 6, cellular/eSIM, AI voice search, and full shortwave/SSB coverage in one unit. Big touchscreen, radio archives, and sound quality that beats every other portable I've tested.

~$349
This is the exact unit we tested — no guessing which listing or variant to buy.

Specifications

Display3.5" high-resolution touchscreen
BandsFM, AM/MW, SW, SSB
ConnectivityWi-Fi 6 (2.4GHz + 5GHz, WPA3), 4G/eSIM/SIM slot, Bluetooth
Stations40,000+ internet radio stations and podcasts, plus radio archive playback
AI FeaturesVoice search, AI assistant
BatteryReplaceable 18650
ColorsBlack, Silver

Pros

  • The screen is genuinely one of the best on any portable radio at this price point — big, sharp, and easy to navigate, and it's a real step up from the smaller mono displays most portables ship with
  • Internet radio done right — Wi-Fi streaming across 40,000+ stations opens up content no standalone shortwave radio can touch, and WiFi 6 (2.4/5GHz) means it streams fast and buffer-free both indoors and out
  • Radio archives are a standout feature — being able to go back and catch a broadcast you missed isn't something I've seen on anything else in this category
  • Voice search actually works — say what you want to listen to (even a shorthand like "BBC") and it pulls up the matching stations fast and accurately
  • FM RDS is excellent — station name and song info pop up quickly and reliably
  • Sound quality is noticeably better than other portables I've tested — the 3-driver 10W speaker gives it real depth and volume, especially on FM, not tinny like most radios this size
  • Bass control is genuinely strong — noticeably better low-end than either the Tecsun PL990X or ChoYong's own previous LC90 model
  • MW/FM/LW sensitivity is legitimately competitive with the Tecsun PL990X thanks to the TEF6686 chip paired with the SI4735 — this isn't just an internet radio with a weak analog tuner bolted on
  • Doubles as a Bluetooth speaker, and SD card music playback is simple — the on-screen file browser makes finding your own tracks painless
  • Sharp overall design — big, bold rotary dials, clear button labeling, and a build quality that's been compared favorably to radios like the Icom IC-705
  • Firmware updates have come quickly since launch — ChoYong pushed a meaningful update addressing early user feedback not long after release, so this radio is actively improving
  • Still genuinely portable despite the feature set — this is a radio you can take with you, not just a desk unit

Cons

  • MW/AM DXing isn't this radio's strongest suit — it's solid for casual listening, but a dedicated DX radio will still out-pull it on the weakest signals
  • Shortwave tuning read slightly off in my testing, even with the offset adjustment in settings — worth checking against a known frequency after a firmware update, since ChoYong has been fixing issues quickly
  • Some users doing SSB/ham listening have reported a faint "chuffing" noise while tuning shortwave; the AM Squelch setting helps but can pull down audio levels if pushed too far — hopefully addressed in a future update
  • The antenna's 3.5mm connector is on the delicate side — ChoYong recommends using a lightweight patch cable rather than yanking on it, which is a minor extra thing to keep in mind
  • The antenna itself only articulates up and down, not side-to-side, so peaking a weak signal takes a bit more patience than on radios with a fully adjustable mount
  • No airband coverage built in, and no flip-stand or carry case included at this price point — small omissions on an otherwise premium-feeling flagship
  • Best thought of as an all-around smart radio first and a dedicated DX machine second — if weak-signal shortwave/AM DXing is your main hobby, pair this with a good external antenna or keep a dedicated DX radio alongside it

Verdict

Thanks to Flora and the team at ChoYong for sending the LC100 out for review — this is one of the most ambitious radios I've tested, and it mostly delivers on that ambition.

If you want one device that handles internet radio, FM, and shortwave without carrying three separate radios, the LC100 is a strong pick. The screen, the sound quality, the radio archive feature, and the voice search all make it feel like a genuinely different category of radio rather than just another portable with Wi-Fi bolted on. I especially came away impressed by the archive feature — nothing else I've reviewed lets you go back and catch something you missed. The receiver side held up better than I expected too, with MW/FM sensitivity that's genuinely in the same conversation as the Tecsun PL990X.

The traditional shortwave/AM DXing experience is where it's a step behind a dedicated DX radio — MW performance is good but not exceptional, the shortwave tuning read slightly off in my testing, and the antenna's limited articulation makes it a little more work to peak a weak signal. None of these felt like dealbreakers to me, more like the trade-offs you'd expect from a radio doing this many things at once, and ChoYong has already shown it moves fast on firmware fixes since launch.

Bottom line: this is the best all-around smart radio I've tested, not the best dedicated DX radio, and it doesn't really need to be — it's doing a different job well. For most listeners who want variety, convenience, and genuinely good sound in one device, it earns a 7.7/10. I'll revisit this rating as ChoYong continues shipping firmware updates.
